title: Idolatry
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Idolatry is replacing the living God with created things, desires, people, power, comfort, self, or false worship. It is not only bowing to images, but giving ultimate trust, love, fear, or obedience to anything besides God.
summary: Idolatry is replacing the living God with created things, desires, people, power, comfort, self, or false worship. It is not only bowing to images, but giving ultimate trust, love, fear, or obedience to anything besides God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ restores true worship by reconciling sinners to God and freeing them from idols. In Him, believers turn from false gods to serve the living and true God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Idolatry begins when people exchange the glory of God for created things. This can involve carved images, false religions, possessions, pleasure, approval, power, family, comfort, ministry, control, or self.

Idols promise life but enslave the heart. What a person worships will shape desires, fears, decisions, sacrifices, and identity. Idolatry is therefore not a minor mistake; it is misplaced worship.

Scripture connects idolatry with sinful desires. Covetousness is called idolatry because the heart begins treating what it wants as ultimate. A person may reject visible idols while still being ruled by invisible ones.

Christ frees people from idols by restoring them to the living God. The Gospel calls sinners to turn from false masters and find life, forgiveness, satisfaction, and hope in God through Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people do not think they struggle with idolatry because they do not bow before statues. Scripture goes deeper, exposing the things the heart trusts, serves, fears, and loves more than God.

This doctrine helps believers understand why good things become destructive when made ultimate. Recovery, relationships, ministry, comfort, success, or approval can become idols if they take the place only God deserves.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask God to expose what rules your heart. Notice what you fear losing, what you run to for life, and what you obey at the cost of faithfulness. Turn from idols to Christ, and worship the living God with your trust, desires, decisions, and obedience.
